title: Starting and finishing
about: Phrasal verbs for starting things (set about a job, set out on a journey, start out as a nurse, from the outset) and for finishing or stopping them (call off, break off, finish off, polish off, pack up, give up, cut down, wind down, fizzle out, dry up).

items.pattern: set about sth / set about doing sth · with an object, not separable: set about the job / set about it, never set it about · followed by -ing, not to: set about cleaning · set – set – set · objects: a task, the housework, repairing sth, a problem
items.meaning: start a job or task, especially one that needs a lot of time or effort
items.example: The garage was full of junk, so on Saturday we **set about** clearing it.
more: As soon as she got home, she **set about** cooking dinner for ten people.
How should I **set about** finding a good dentist in a new town?
items.watchOut: «Взятися за прибирання» — set about cleaning (з -ing), не set about to clean і не take for cleaning (калька з «взятися за»). Не плутай з set out (вирушити в дорогу) і set up (заснувати, встановити). Форми однакові: set – set – set.

items.pattern: set out (on a journey / for a place / from a place) · intransitive · set – set – set · usually a long or planned journey: set out on a trip, set out for the coast, set out at dawn · very close to set off
items.meaning: leave a place and begin a journey
items.example: We **set out** for the mountains at five o'clock to miss the traffic.
more: The walkers **set out** in sunshine, but it was pouring by midday.
My parents **set out** on a tour of Italy the day after their wedding.
items.watchOut: Вирушити — set out або set off, майже однаково. Не went out: go out — вийти з дому, піти розважитися. Set out to do sth — інше значення: мати намір щось зробити (She set out to win the race).

items.pattern: start out / start off (as sth / in sth / doing sth) · intransitive · about the first stage of a career, a life or a business: start out as a waiter, start off in a small flat · often followed by but / later / then
items.meaning: begin your working life, a career or an existence in a particular way, often different from how things are later
items.example: My grandad **started out** as a bus driver and ended up managing the whole depot.
more: Our village shop **started off** as a tiny kiosk next to the bus stop.
Like most young couples, they **started out** in a rented one-room flat.
items.watchOut: «Починав офіціантом» — started out AS a waiter (as, не like і не from). Start out і start off тут означають те саме. Не плутай зі start up — заснувати бізнес або завести двигун.

items.pattern: noun, always with the: at the outset (of sth), from the outset · from the verb set out · a little formal; in everyday speech also from the start
items.uk: початок; від самого початку (from the outset)
items.example: It was clear from **the outset** that the new boss and I wouldn't get on.
more: Tell your builder at **the outset** how much you can spend.
The holiday went wrong from **the outset**: our flight was cancelled.
items.watchOut: Завжди з the: from the outset, at the outset. Наголос на першому складі: OUTset. Не плутай з upset (засмучений) і outcome (результат).

items.pattern: call sth off · with an object, separable: call off the match / call the match off / call it off, never call off it · often passive: be called off · objects: a match, a strike, a wedding, a trip, a search, building work · close to cancel
items.meaning: decide that something planned will not happen, or stop something that has already started
items.example: The concert was **called off** at the last minute because the singer was ill.
more: We had to **call off** the barbecue when it started to pour.
They planned a big anniversary party, but they **called it off** when Grandma went into hospital.
items.watchOut: Займенник — посередині: call it off, не call off it. Не плутай з put off — відкласти на потім: called off — не буде взагалі, put off — буде пізніше. Call back — передзвонити, call up — зателефонувати.

items.pattern: sth dries up · intransitive · subjects: money, funding, work, orders, customers, offers of help · often continuous: the money is drying up · literally: a river or a well dries up
items.meaning: (of money, work or supplies) stop coming, so there is none left
items.uk: вичерпатися, перестати надходити (про гроші, роботу, замовлення)
items.example: When the tourists stopped coming, work for the local taxi drivers **dried up**.
more: The little theatre closed when its funding **dried up**.
In summer the orders **dry up**, so we take our holiday in July.
items.watchOut: Dry up — джерело перестало давати (the funding dried up). Run out (of sth) — ми самі все витратили (we ran out of money). Буквально dry up — пересохнути (про річку, колодязь); dry up the dishes — витерти посуд.

items.pattern: break off · intransitive: break off for lunch, break off in the middle of a sentence · or break off sth, separable: break off a conversation / break it off · broke – broken
items.meaning: suddenly stop doing or saying something, often for a short time
items.example: The painters **broke off** for a sandwich at midday.
more: She **broke off** in the middle of a sentence when her boss walked in.
Grandad **broke off** his story to answer the phone.
items.watchOut: Break off — перерватися (break off for lunch). Не плутай: break down — зламатися, break up — розійтися (про пару) або піти на канікули, break out — спалахнути (про пожежу, війну). Break off an engagement — розірвати заручини. Буквально break off — відламати(ся).

items.pattern: finish sth off · with an object, separable: finish off the job / finish the job off / finish it off, never finish off it · objects: a job, the painting, a report; also food and drink: finish off the soup
items.meaning: complete the last part of something
items.example: It took us two weekends to **finish off** the fence round the garden.
more: Let's **finish off** the cake before it goes stale.
She stayed late at the office to **finish off** the monthly report.
items.watchOut: Finish off підкреслює саме останню частину: доробити, доїсти, допити. Займенник посередині: finish it off, не finish off it.

items.pattern: polish sth off · informal · with an object, separable: polish off a pizza / polish a pizza off / polish it off · objects: food and drink (a cake, a bottle of lemonade), or a piece of work
items.meaning: finish something quickly and easily, especially eat all of some food
items.example: The kids **polished off** a whole tray of pancakes before I'd even sat down.
more: Dad **polished off** all the jobs on his list before lunch.
Between the four of us, we **polished off** two big bottles of lemonade.
items.watchOut: Це не про полірування! Розм.: швидко й легко доїсти або доробити. Займенник посередині: polished it off. polish (полірувати) і Polish (польський) різняться лише великою літерою і звучать по-різному: /ˈpɒlɪʃ/ і /ˈpəʊlɪʃ/.

items.pattern: pack up · intransitive: pack up and go home · or pack sth up, separable: pack up your things / pack your things up / pack them up · usually at the end of the working day or after an activity · BrE informal: a machine packs up = it breaks down
items.meaning: put your things together and get ready to leave, usually after finishing something
items.uk: зібрати речі (і піти), закінчити й зібратися (після роботи)
items.example: The beach was getting cold, so we **packed up** and went back to the hotel.
more: The builders **pack up** at four, so the noise stops early.
Can you help me **pack up** the picnic things? It's starting to rain.
items.watchOut: Pack up — зібрати речі й закінчити (роботу, пікнік). Просто pack — пакувати валізу (I need to pack for the trip). Розм. брит.: my old car has packed up — зламалася. Pack it in (розм.) — кинути (роботу, заняття).

items.pattern: give sth up / give up doing sth · with an object, separable: give up sugar / give sugar up / give it up, never give up it · followed by -ing, not to: give up smoking · gave – given · objects: a habit, a food or drink, smoking, meat
items.meaning: stop doing or having something, usually a habit
items.example: My sister **gave up** meat when she was fifteen.
more: I'm going to **give up** fizzy drinks for the whole of January.
He tried to **give up** smoking three times before he finally managed it.
items.watchOut: «Кинути палити» — give up smoking (з -ing), не give up to smoke і не throw smoking. Займенник посередині: give it up. Stop to smoke — зупинитися, щоб покурити, тобто навпаки.

items.pattern: cut down (on sth) · intransitive; what you reduce comes after on: cut down on sugar, cut down on meat · cut down to sth: to two cups a day · with no object: I'm trying to cut down · close to cut back (on sth)
items.meaning: eat, drink or use less of something
items.example: Since we **cut down on** meat, our shopping bills have got smaller.
more: The doctor says I should **cut down on** coffee if I want to sleep better.
I used to eat crisps every evening, but I've **cut down** to once a week.
items.watchOut: «Їсти менше цукру» — cut down on sugar: потрібне on. Без on cut down sth часто означає «зрубати» (cut down a tree). Cut down — зменшити, cut out — зовсім прибрати (cut out sugar), give up — кинути.

items.pattern: wind down · intransitive · after work, after a busy day, before bed · wind – wound – wound /waʊnd/ · close to relax, unwind
items.meaning: gradually relax after a tiring or stressful time
items.example: After a long shift, Olena **winds down** with a hot bath and an audiobook.
more: We spent the first two days of the holiday by the pool, just **winding down**.
Turn off the TV an hour before bed to help the kids **wind down**.
items.watchOut: Вимова: wind тут /waɪnd/, як find, а не /wɪnd/ (вітер). Минулий час — wound /waʊnd/. Wind up — інше: закінчити (зустріч), опинитися десь або дражнити когось. Calm down — заспокоїтися (після злості чи паніки), а wind down — розслабитися після втоми.

items.pattern: sth fizzles out · intransitive, no object · subjects: interest, enthusiasm, a plan, a protest, a relationship, a storm · often with soon, gradually, after a while · a little informal
items.meaning: gradually end or disappear, usually in a disappointing way
items.example: We all promised to go swimming every Saturday, but our enthusiasm **fizzled out** after a fortnight.
more: My interest in learning the piano **fizzled out** after a few weeks.
The party **fizzled out** at about ten, when most people went home.
items.watchOut: Fizzle out — завжди без додатка: the plan fizzled out, не they fizzled out the plan. Це про те, що згасає поступово й розчаровує. Не плутай з break out — спалахнути, початися (про пожежу, війну).

items.pattern: give up · intransitive: Don't give up! · or give up sth / give up doing sth, separable: give it up · give up on sb/sth: stop hoping that sb/sth will succeed · usually because something is too difficult or takes too long
items.meaning: stop trying to do something before you finish it, usually because it is too difficult
items.uk: здатися, опустити руки; кинути (не довівши до кінця)
items.example: The crossword was too difficult, so I **gave up** and looked at the answers.
more: She failed her driving test twice but didn't **give up**.
After an hour of trying to fix the tap, Dad **gave up** and called a plumber.
items.watchOut: «Не здавайся!» — Don't give up! Surrender — здатися ворогові, у звичайному житті так не кажуть. Give in — поступитися (комусь або спокусі): I gave in and bought the cake. Займенник посередині: gave it up.

warmup.uk: Мій тато кинув палити десять років тому.
warmup.q: My dad ___ smoking ten years ago.
warmup.explain: Кинути звичку — give up + -ing. Throw — кинути предмет; give off — виділяти (запах, тепло).
Менше їсти чи пити чогось — cut down on sth. Cut off — відрізати, відключити.

warmup.uk: Після роботи мені потрібна година, щоб розслабитися.
warmup.q: After work I need an hour to ___.
warmup.explain: Wind down — поступово розслабитися. Wind up — закінчити щось або дражнити когось; relax down не кажуть.

warmup.uk: Щойно гості пішли, вона взялася мити посуд.
warmup.q: As soon as the guests left, she ___ washing the dishes.
warmup.explain: Взятися за справу — set about + -ing. Took for — калька з «взялася за»; set out — вирушити в дорогу.

warmup.q: The picnic was ___ because of the rain.
warmup.explain: Скасувати — call off (або просто cancel, без off). Call out — вигукнути.

warmup.uk: Ми вирушили о шостій ранку, щоб не стояти в заторах.
warmup.q: We ___ at six in the morning to avoid the traffic.
warmup.explain: Вирушити в дорогу — set out (або set off). Set about — взятися за справу; set in — настати (про погоду, зиму).

warmup.uk: Він починав офіціантом, а тепер має власний ресторан.
warmup.q: He ___ as a waiter, and now he owns a restaurant.
warmup.explain: Починати (кар'єру) як… — start out as (або start off as). Start up — заснувати бізнес, завести двигун.

warmup.uk: Я від самого початку знала, що це погана ідея.
warmup.q: I knew from the ___ that it was a bad idea.
warmup.explain: From the outset — від самого початку (іменник від set out). Upset — засмучений.

A.q: After breakfast, Mum ___ the huge pile of ironing.
A.explain: Set about sth — взятися за справу, яка потребує часу й сил. Set off — вирушити або (ненароком) запустити сигналізацію; set up — заснувати, встановити.

A.q: We ___ before sunrise to reach the lake by noon.
A.explain: Set out — вирушити в дорогу. Set about потребує додатка (set about the job); start up — заснувати бізнес або завести двигун.

A.q: When she was nineteen, my sister ___ as a hairdresser, and now she owns three salons.
A.explain: Start out as… — починати (кар'єру) як… Set about — взятися за справу; start up — заснувати бізнес, завести двигун.

B.q: The tennis final was ___ because of the rain.
B.explain: Call off — скасувати. Call out — вигукнути; polish off — швидко доїсти або доробити.

B.q: The doctor told Grandad to ___ salt.
B.explain: Менше їсти чи пити чогось — cut down on sth (з on). Cut off — відрізати, відключити.

B.q: A hot bath helps me ___ after a long day.
B.explain: Wind down — розслабитися після напруженого дня. Dry up — перестати надходити (про гроші, роботу); fizzle out — поступово зійти нанівець.

example.title: Sam's garden
example.uk:
Минулої весни мій брат Сем вирішив вирощувати власні овочі. Він узявся за справу з величезною енергією і від самого початку працював у саду щовечора. Однієї суботи він рано вирушив до садового центру й повернувся з насінням, інструментами та крихітною теплицею.

Проте за кілька тижнів його запал почав згасати. Кілька днів поспіль ішов дощ, а друзі скоро перестали пропонувати допомогу. Він мало не здався, але сусід йому не дозволив.

Тепер щовечора Сем складає інструменти, заварює собі чай і сидить у саду, щоб відпочити. Минулого тижня ми за десять хвилин умолотили його перші помідори. Він навіть став їсти менше солодкого!
example.en:
Last spring my brother Sam decided to grow his own vegetables. He [[set about|a1]] the job with huge energy, and from [[the outset|a4]] he worked in the garden every evening. One Saturday he [[set out|a2]] early for the garden centre and came back with seeds, tools and a tiny greenhouse.

After a few weeks, though, his enthusiasm began to [[fizzle out|b10]]. It rained for days, and his friends' offers of help soon [[dried up|b2]]. He nearly [[gave up|b11]], but his neighbour wouldn't let him.

Now, every evening, Sam [[packs up|b6]] his tools, makes a cup of tea and sits in the garden to [[wind down|b9]]. Last week we [[polished off|b5]] his first tomatoes in ten minutes. He has even [[cut down on|b8]] sweets!
